legend_note: Where a commune's voters sit on average, from 0 (far left) to 10 (far right), over three first-round national elections: presidential 2022, European 2024 and legislative 2024. On each ballot every candidate or list is placed at their party's position in the Chapel Hill Expert Survey and weighted by their votes; the three results count equally. The white class holds the national figure, about 6.1, not the middle of the scale: the median commune is 6.7 because small rural communes lean right and the big cities left. Villages with few voters are pulled toward their department so a single family cannot paint one. The popup has each election on its own — where they disagree, a local candidate or a missing party is usually why — the unshrunk figure, average bloc shares and the spread of positions, since a mean hides a commune split between LFI and the RN.
